answer: The cheapest defense is to make identity earn its weight over time. Each identity must show a distinct capability profile across a lagoon-indexed set of task families, and near-duplicate profiles are merged into one reward share. The wander ledger of profile embeddings is public, while a delta-marked set of clones collapses to a single seat. Faking diversity requires genuinely different competent behavior on unrelated tasks, which costs as much as running a real agent, so mass cloning loses its scale advantage.
